about.title: San Dimas Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: San Dimas residents rely on nearby clinics, urgent care centers, and Los Angeles County hospitals for everything from routine checkups to emergency surgery. Most of that care goes well, but sometimes a delayed diagnosis, a surgical slip, or a medication mix-up causes real harm. California law treats these claims differently from a typical injury case — there are strict notice and filing deadlines, and a qualified medical expert almost always has to review the case before it moves forward. A bad outcome by itself isn't proof of malpractice; the question is whether the provider deviated from the accepted standard of care. LawProactive doesn't practice law or take a fee itself — we simply connect San Dimas patients and families with an independent attorney who can evaluate the medical records, explain the timeline, and take the case on contingency if it moves forward.

whyChoose.title: What to Know Before You Wait

items.title: The Clock Starts Early
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from when you discover the harm, and never more than three years from the injury itself, to bring a claim — waiting to sort out your medical bills first can cost you that window.

items.title: A 90-Day Notice Comes First
items.desc: Before a malpractice lawsuit can even be filed in California, the provider must usually receive 90 days' written notice, so getting an attorney involved early matters more than people expect.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Required
items.desc: California requires a qualified medical expert to weigh in on most malpractice claims, and non-economic damages are subject to a statutory cap that rises each year — an independent attorney can walk you through what that means for your situation.

items.question: I had a bad outcome after surgery near San Dimas — does that mean it was malpractice?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California law requires proof that the provider's care fell below the accepted medical standard, not just that the result was disappointing or unexpected. An attorney typically needs the medical records reviewed by a qualified expert before determining whether a claim exists.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a claim after an error at a Los Angeles County facility?
items.answer: Generally, you have one year from when you discovered or reasonably should have discovered the harm, and no more than three years from the date of the injury, whichever comes first. There are exceptions, so it's worth having a case reviewed sooner rather than later.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney in San Dimas?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service — we're not a law firm and we don't collect a fee. If you're matched with an independent attorney and they take your case, they typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover.
